note: Per-row notes for the Verified shortlist page. Every statement is taken from the official page recorded in data/cross-checks.json for the same row; nothing is inferred. Written by arena/7a477419-own1 on 2026-11-02.

rows.note: Built for AI bots: "This is a bot-only competition". No purchase or fee to participate (Metaculus rules), but bot LLM/search costs are yours; free AskNews search for registered bot makers and donated LLM credits only for select applicants. $50,000 pool on the tournament page; the resources page says $58k+ every 4 months across the seasonal tournament, MiniBench and Market Pulse.

Official page: "Internet access is not available during Kaggle evaluation (no API-based systems like GPT/Claude/etc.)"; all prizes require open-source, reproducible solutions. An AI agent can help write code, but the submitted solution cannot call hosted models.
Event page: the project must connect to Twitch and be "built with OpenAI Codex"; entry requires the Codex session ID, a repository URL and a public YouTube demo (max 3 minutes).

Forecasting tournament, not a coding task: $10,000 pool, closes 2026-11-04. Metaculus rules: no purchase or fee; bots are ineligible for prizes, but humans may use AI tools to assist if the final forecasts reflect their own decisions and understanding.

Rules page (read 2026-11-01 by another session): no purchase necessary; a functional demo and a public source repository are required. Headline $67,500 on the event page mixes cash and non-cash prizes (flag I-20); the rules itemise $12,000 for first place. Whether AI tools are permitted was not re-read.

The task is to build a coding agent: submission is an agent.yaml config on a single allowed Gemma 4 variant (no mixing models), scored by PASS/FAIL on SWE-Bench-style patches. Ideal topic for an agent team, but a hosted frontier model cannot be the submitted agent.
Must be built with Kiro (IDE, CLI, Web or Kiro Crew); repo must contain a /.kiro directory and an open-source licence; new project built after 2026-10-30; demo video under 3 minutes.

Overview: "you will use AI coding agents, classical optimization, and algorithmic insights in a closed verification loop"; "No quantum physics background or quantum hardware is required." Mid-competition $10,000 milestone on 2026-11-20 requires a public notebook.
Notebook submissions only, internet disabled, 9-hour CPU/GPU limit; predictions are ranked SMILES lists scored by MRR@25.
Notebook submissions only, internet disabled, 9-hour limit; winner must license the submission under an OSI-approved open-source licence.

Must be a Forge app integrating an Atlassian product; bonus categories include Best Agents (Rovo) and Best app with Atlassian MCP at $1,500 × 6 each. Needs a free Atlassian developer licence, an installation link and a public YouTube demo.
Judged analytics writeup (≤ 2,000 words, public Kaggle Notebook); not a leaderboard. University Track is undergraduate-only. Must use the player-tracking data to be scored.

Open optimisation problem scored by a published formula; the page names simulated annealing, gradient descent, evolutionary and reinforcement-learning methods. Two $5,000 milestone prizes (2027-01-17, 2027-04-18). No restriction on tooling was read; rules page not read in this pass.

HeroX guidelines: "Institutions, companies, nonprofit organizations, and individuals based in the United States are eligible to compete." Two rounds, prizes from $15,000 to $100,000. No entry fee was stated on the pages read; the official rules PDF could not be fetched. Closing time differs between pages (5 PM ET vs 23:59 UTC on 2026-12-03).
Free, but only for students aged 14–18 in teams of 2–4 with a supervising teacher. AI tools are "allowed and expected". Registration closes 13 Nov (23:59 AoE).
